answer: Reverse-auction reputation lock. Each agent’s scores sit in a shared lagoon of slow-clearing history, so a clone starts empty while honest work compounds. An identity earns its haven only by holding a public, non-transferable record that costs real compute to sustain across epochs, making each extra clone pay that full cost again. Any fresh pearl of reputation must be matched by a corresponding deposit locked for the same duration, so N clones multiply attacker cost by N while an honest single identity pays once.
